item.title: How Innovations Shaped Light Rail in Europe: Implications Regarding Social Acceptance and Urban Integration
item.dc:title: How Innovations Shaped Light Rail in Europe: Implications Regarding Social Acceptance and Urban Integration
item.dc:creator: Pablo Rico-Pinazo Daniel Navas-Carrillo María José Márquez-Ballesteros Department of Art and Architecture, University of Málaga, Málaga, SpainPablo Rico-Pinazo is a predoctoral fellow in urban and regional planning at the University of Málaga. His PhD thesis will focus on the suitability of light rail systems to medium-sized European cities and their role impact on the quality of public space.Daniel Navas-Carrillo is an associate professor in urban and regional planning. He is an architect and member of the research group Heritage and Territorial Urban Development in Andalusia (HUM700) and the University Institute Habitat, Territory, and Digitalization (iHTD). He also serves as Deputy Vice-Rector for Postgraduate and Own Studies at the University of Málaga.María José Márquez-Ballesteros is an associate professor in urban and regional planning at the University of Málaga. She has directed various research projects financed by the Spanish Ministry of Ecological Transition, serves as a member of the Habitat, Territory and Digitalization Research Institute, and currently collaborates with Fundación Renovables in the development of initiatives, projects and consultancies on the transition towards a new, fairer, more sustainable and more human energy model.

item.title: Metabolic Infrastructure Dysfunction: The Case of Composting in Mexico City
item.dc:title: Metabolic Infrastructure Dysfunction: The Case of Composting in Mexico City
item.dc:creator: Andrea Bortolotti Louise Guibrunet a Department of Architecture and Urban Studies, Polytechnic University of Milan, Milan, Italyb Institute of Geography, National Autonomous University of Mexico, Mexico City, MexicoAndrea Bortolotti is an assistant professor at the Department of Architecture and Urban Studies, Polytechnic University of Milan. His research interests concern urban metabolism, the circular economy, and their relationship to urban policy and planning. He has worked on organic waste and construction and demolition waste in the contexts of Brussels and Milan.Louise Guibrunet is a researcher at the Institute of Geography, National Autonomous University of Mexico. Her research interests are urban sustainability and urban metabolism, focusing on urban waste management and food systems. She has researched both topics in the context of Mexico City.
